clue.text: One who works by hand gives strain. to a politician from the London area

parts.note: SE is the postcode district for south-east London
an MP is a Member of Parliament
strain and stress are synonyms

explanation.surface: A manual worker passes the pressure on to a local London MP.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the postcode for south-east London. The stray full stop after 'strain' is a printing blemish; 'gives' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress, in an older spelling, sews by hand for a living.

clue.text: The prophet turns up for a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet appears and asks for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses AMOS, the Old Testament prophet, giving the letters for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soma was the ritual intoxicating drink of the ancient Vedic religion.

clue.text: A man with a drink inside is company

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as a drink goes inside a person

parts.note: a man is a male
a nip is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A fellow who has had a tipple is good company.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal is 'inside'. 'Company' is not the social sense but a military unit, which is what misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple was a subdivision of a Roman legion, roughly a company of soldiers.

clue.text: Performer who puts painting up in view with a sound of sea and mountain

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another, as the painting sits in the view

parts.note: a view is a sight

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up reads it from the bottom

parts.note: painting is art

indicators.note: the letter C is said the same as the word sea

parts.note: the word sea is said like the letter C
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: An actor hangs a picture with a vista of sea and mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ART to TRA, and 'in' puts it into SIGHT. Then A, C (which 'sound of' gets from the word sea) and TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight actor performs serious drama rather than comedy or musicals.

clue.text: Abstains from music

explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from something; refrains are also the repeated choruses of a song.

clue.text: Author who sounds as if he is a budding one

indicators.note: says the writer's name is said the same as another word

parts.note: a shoot is a young budding stem

explanation.surface: A writer whose name suggests he is a promising newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevil Shute wrote A Town Like Alice and On the Beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was an English novelist, writer of On the Beach.

clue.text: Strikes back in a fight

indicators.note: the word for strikes is read backwards

parts.note: raps are sharp blows

explanation.surface: Someone hits back during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a practice bout of boxing, a minor fight.

clue.text: Be stimulating and demonstrate the truth without approval

indicators.note: in the old sense outside: one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to prove is to show something is true
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Being thought-provoking means showing the truth even when nobody approves.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so nothing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke is to stir up or stimulate a reaction.

clue.text: Being in the same suit, they cause embarrassment at court

definitions.text: Being in the same suit, they cause embarrassment at court

parts.words: Being in the same suit, they cause embarrassment at court
parts.note: a poker hand of top cards all of one suit, read as royal red faces

explanation.surface: Matching courtiers turn red with shame at the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker the best hand is ace to ten of one suit; read literally, it is a monarch's blush at court.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker this hand is ace, king, queen, jack and ten all in one suit; whimsically, a blush in the royal court.

clue.text: Possessions which bring someone gold

parts.note: a man is someone
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Wealth that brings a person riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a landed estate, a large holding of property.

clue.text: Quarrel with a politician concerning type of tenure

parts.note: a feud is a long quarrel
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A row with a Conservative over a matter of land holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudatory means relating to holding land from a lord under the feudal system.

clue.text: When newly married I chant for the priest

indicators.note: the words are made anew, rearranged into fresh order

explanation.surface: A newlywed sings out for the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges MARRIED, I and CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An archimandrite is a senior abbot or cleric in the Orthodox Church.

clue.text: It is the place of instruction to keep soldiers calm, we hear

indicators.note: the words are said out loud to suggest another phrase

parts.note: privates cool: ordinary soldiers kept cool

explanation.surface: A school exists to stop the troops panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: Privates are ordinary soldiers; keeping them calm is 'privates cool', which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private school is a fee-paying establishment of education.

clue.text: Dispose of some property in Cumbria

parts.note: to sell is to dispose of
a, meaning one or some
a field is a piece of land owned

explanation.surface: Selling off a piece of land in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Sellafield is a nuclear site in Cumbria, a county in north-west England; the definition points to a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellafield is a nuclear plant on the Cumbrian coast, a place located in that county.

clue.text: The plane crash is caused by a heavy creature

indicators.note: a crash smashes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An air disaster blamed on a hefty animal on the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges THE PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant is the heaviest land animal.

clue.text: Changes about in being like a cone

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

parts.note: a peal is a set of changes rung on bells

explanation.surface: Someone changes their views while turning into something cone-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' is a bell-ringing term, a series of changes rung being a peal; 'about' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineal means shaped like a pine cone, as the pineal gland is.

clue.text: Where to express displeasure about part of the course being taken up

indicators.note: one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to frown is to show displeasure

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards

parts.note: a tee is part of a golf course

explanation.surface: Someone frowns crossly where part of a course is being dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal 'being taken up' turns the golf word upwards and 'about' wraps the frown round it. 'Where' defines a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Freetown is the capital city of Sierra Leone, a location.

clue.text: Seaman who gives a mark to a beginner

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner driver plates
a scar is a mark on the skin

explanation.surface: A sailor marks a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is an Indian or South-East Asian sailor serving on European ships.

clue.text: Punishment as a sign of rank

explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are both strokes of the lash and the chevrons showing military grade.

clue.text: Beats her badly, but shows signs of life

indicators.note: the letters are put together in a poor, disordered way

explanation.surface: A man beats a woman cruelly, yet she survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges BEATS HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inhales and exhales is alive.

clue.text: Brave girl in this place holding nothing in

indicators.note: one word holds the others within it

parts.note: here means in this place
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A courageous girl here holds nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal is 'holding'; the first 'in' belongs to the phrase meaning here, the second gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is a woman admired for courage.

clue.text: The one who finishes off an aristocrat behind the trees is new to crime

definitions.note: describes the person, where the answer is a noun for such a person

indicators.note: the aristocrat and finisher come after the trees

parts.note: firs are conifers
toff is British slang for an upper-class person
an ender is one who ends something

explanation.surface: A killer who polishes off a nobleman behind the woods is a novice criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal 'behind' puts the aristocrat and finisher after the trees. Toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: A first offender is someone convicted for the first time, a novice lawbreaker.

clue.text: Bird places foot on island

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A bird sets its foot on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts F above INCH in this down clue. Inch is a Scottish term for an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch is a small seed-eating songbird.

clue.text: Poems held in good esteem

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of words

explanation.surface: Verses are highly regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' reveals the run inside gooD ESteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Language in which noun operates strangely

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an odd, unexpected way

explanation.surface: A language in which a noun behaves oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges N and OPERATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international tongue devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: I competed like Bacchus

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: I contested something in the style of the wine god.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacchus, Roman god of wine, is pictured wearing an ivy wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is shown crowned with ivy leaves, so he is ivy-covered.

clue.text: Run for the line.

explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a sprint, and also a punctuation stroke.

clue.text: Constant spirit shown in the game

indicators.note: one word is displayed inside the other

parts.note: chess is a board game
an angel is a heavenly spirit

explanation.surface: A steady spirit appears in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal is 'shown in'; the game is the board game, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Changeless means never varying, steady.
